ueber.text:
CAM Addon {version}

Makes FreeCAD CAM easier to use.

So far: describe a machine as an assembly – axes, spindles, tool and workpiece mounts –, move it by hand, hand it over to CAM, check whether its travel suffices for the paths of a CAM job, let it run through them and check for collisions. Tool manager with holders, a material list, cutting data per material and use case, a comparison of strategies and a planner for roughing values; spindle speed, feed, step over and step down into the CAM job. 4-axis machining: place a part at the front of a round bar, centred (rotary axis A, B or C).

License: LGPL-2.1-or-later

sprachwahl.frage: Which language should the CAM Addon speak?
sprachwahl.hinweis: You can change this at any time: Edit → Preferences → CAM Addon.
einstellungen.sprache.neustart: The new language fully applies after restarting FreeCAD.
kette.gelenk_ohne_teile: The joint “{gelenk}” does not connect two parts of this assembly and is skipped.
kette.gelenkart_nicht_unterstuetzt: The joint “{gelenk}” is of type “{art}”. Machines only use Fixed, Slider and Revolute joints – this joint is skipped.
kette.kein_festes_teil: No part is grounded. Ground the machine bed in the assembly so it is clear what stands still.
kette.koerper_lose: The body “{koerper}” is not attached to any joint. It will stay behind when the machine moves.
kette.gelenk_im_glied: The joint “{gelenk}” sits between two bodies that are already rigidly connected – it cannot move.
kette.geschlossene_schleife: The joint “{gelenk}” closes the chain into a loop. Machine chains must be open (from the bed to the tool or workpiece) – this joint is skipped.
kette.glied_haengt_nicht_am_bett: The bodies “{koerper}” are not connected to the grounded machine bed by any joint.
kette.doppelt_gelagert: “{gelenk}” connects the same parts a second time, like “{erstes}”. The assembly cannot solve that – the parts will jump. An axis needs only one joint, even if it sits in two bearings: suppress or delete “{gelenk}”. The second bearing block still stays fixed to the bed.
eigenschaft.maschine.typ: Marker by which the CAM Addon recognises its machine object.
eigenschaft.gelenk: The assembly joint this operating mode belongs to.
eigenschaft.art: Linear (travels), Positioning (turns to an angle) or Spindle (turns at a speed).
eigenschaft.ncname: Name of the axis in the NC program, e.g. X1, C4 or S4.
eigenschaft.vorschubmax: Maximum cutting feed in mm/min. 0 = unknown.
eigenschaft.beschleunigung: Acceleration: linear in m/s², rotary in rev/s². 0 = unknown.
eigenschaft.ruck: Jerk: linear in m/s³, rotary in rev/s³. 0 = unknown.
eigenschaft.endlos: Does the axis turn endlessly (no end stop)?
eigenschaft.durchmesser: Does the axis count in diameter, like X on a lathe? The add-on then shows twice the value with “Ø” – like the control – and the post processor writes X that way into the program. Calculations use the radius.
eigenschaft.geschwindigkeit: Maximum rotary speed when positioning, in rpm. 0 = unknown.
eigenschaft.drehzahl: Maximum spindle speed in rpm. 0 = unknown.
eigenschaft.hochlaufzeit: Time from standstill to maximum speed in seconds. 0 = unknown.
eigenschaft.lcs: The local coordinate system marking the mount: origin = reference point, Z = direction.
eigenschaft.aufnahmeart: Tool (a tool sits here) or Workpiece (parts are clamped here).
eigenschaft.spindel: For driven tools: the spindle operating mode that turns the tool.
maschine.name_fehlt: “{eintrag}” has no NC name yet (e.g. X1, C4, S4).
maschine.name_doppelt: The NC name “{name}” is used more than once. Each name may only be used once per machine.
maschine.gelenk_fehlt: “{name}” no longer belongs to a joint – the joint was deleted. Assign another joint or delete “{name}”.
maschine.gelenk_keine_achse: “{name}” belongs to the joint “{gelenk}”, which is not an axis of the machine (see the assembly messages).
maschine.art_passt_nicht: “{name}” is set to “{art}”, but “{gelenk}” is the wrong kind of joint for that. Linear only fits slider joints, Positioning and Spindle only revolute joints.
maschine.art_doppelt: The joint “{gelenk}” has the same operating mode twice.
maschine.lcs_fehlt: The mount “{name}” no longer refers to a coordinate system.
maschine.lcs_ausserhalb: The coordinate system of the mount “{name}” is not inside any part of this machine.
maschine.spindel_keine_spindel: The mount “{name}” names a drive that is not a spindle.
maschine.keine_werkzeugaufnahme: There is no tool mount yet. Without one the add-on cannot tell which axes sit in the head.
maschine.keine_werkstueckaufnahme: There is no workpiece mount yet. Without one the add-on cannot tell which axes sit in the table.
maschine.rolle_mehrdeutig: The joint “{gelenk}” moves both a tool and a workpiece. Check that the mounts are in the right parts.
eigenschaft.schaltzeit: Time to index the turret by one station, in seconds. 0 = unknown.
eigenschaft.platz: Station number in the turret (P1, P2, …). 0 = not a turret station.
eigenschaft.bestueckung: Loading: which tool from the tool manager sits in this station (its ID); empty: free. Load it in “Edit machine”.
maschine.revolver_ohne_plaetze: The turret “{name}” has no tool stations yet. Add tool mounts in the turret or use “Distribute stations”.
maschine.plaetze_nummern: The stations of the turret “{name}” have duplicate or missing numbers.
befehl.maschine.tooltip: Turns the assembly into a machine: name the axes, enter their data, define tool and workpiece mounts.
dialog.keine_baugruppe:
There is no assembly here yet.

Quickest: “New machine …” builds a ready-made machine in a new document – a lathe or 3-axis mill with your dimensions, 5-axis mills.

Or build your own: in the Assembly workbench, rough bodies for bed, slides, spindle etc., connected by joints (fixed, slider or revolute). Then run this command again.
dialog.name: Name:
dialog.name.tooltip: Name of the machine as it will be offered in CAM.
dialog.achsen.tooltip: Every slider and revolute joint of the assembly. Below each are its operating modes – e.g. S4 (spindle) and C4 (positioning) on the same joint.
dialog.betriebsart_neu.tooltip: Gives the selected joint an operating mode with an NC name. Only modes that fit the joint type are offered.
dialog.aufnahmen.tooltip: Places where a tool sits or a workpiece is clamped – each marked by a local coordinate system (LCS).
dialog.plaetze_verteilen.tooltip: Creates turret stations P1 … Pn evenly around a circle – starting from a first station.
dialog.bestueckung.tooltip: Which tool from the tool manager sits in this station. A tool sits in at most one station – pick one that is already elsewhere, and the other station becomes free. “– free –” unloads the station; the tool stays in the tool manager.
dialog.bestueckung.keine_plaetze: No turret stations – first add a turret under “Mounts” and use “Distribute stations …”.
dialog.bestueckung.erklaerung: “– free –” unloads a station; the tool stays in the tool manager. A station you do not load holds the tool with its number: T3 in P3.
dialog.werkzeugverwaltung.tooltip: Opens the tool manager. What you save there is available here right away.
dialog.kein_lcs:
The assembly has no local coordinate system (LCS) yet.

In the part where the tool sits or the workpiece is clamped, add an LCS: origin at the reference point (spindle nose, chuck face …), Z axis pointing along the tool or perpendicular to the clamping face.
dialog.glieder.tooltip: Bodies that are rigidly connected and move together. If a body is missing here, it is not attached to any joint.
art.positionieren.beschreibung: turns to an angle (A, B, C …)
art.revolver.beschreibung: indexes from tool station to tool station
verteilen.erklaerung: Choose the first station (an LCS in the turret) and the number of stations. The others are placed evenly around the turret axis and named P1 … Pn. An earlier distribution is replaced.
verteilen.kein_lcs: There is no LCS in the turret yet. Add an LCS for the first station in the turret part.
dialog.noch_keine_betriebsart.tooltip: Select the joint and click “+ Operating mode”. Joints without an operating mode are allowed – they count as adjusted by hand (e.g. a tailstock without an NC axis).
eigenschaft.bezeichnung: Name of the mount, e.g. Chuck or P3.
dialog.beschleunigung_ermitteln: How do I find the acceleration?
export.beschreibung: Created by the CAM Addon from “{dokument}”. Make changes there and hand it over again.
export.rolle_unbekannt: For “{name}” it is unclear whether the axis sits in the table or the head (add tool and workpiece mounts). It was handed over as a table axis.
export.ohne_grenzen: “{name}” has no limits (min/max) on its joint. CAM gets a very large range – enter the limits in the assembly.
export.eine_grenze: “{name}” has only one limit (min or max) on its joint. For the other side CAM gets a very large range – enter both limits in the assembly.
export.wert_bleibt: The CAM definition does not know the {wert} of “{name}” – the value stays stored in the machine.
export.revolver: The CAM definition does not know the turret “{name}” with {anzahl} stations – the stations stay stored in the machine.
export.kette_fehler: FreeCAD reports an error in the axis order: {fehler}
export.eilgang_vorgabe: “{name}” has no rapid traverse – CAM gets FreeCAD's default of {eilgang} {e_vorschub}. Enter the machine's rapid traverse and hand it over again.
export.geschwindigkeit_vorgabe: “{name}” has no speed – CAM gets FreeCAD's default of {geschwindigkeit} rpm. Enter the machine's speed and hand it over again.
export.drehzahl_fehlt: “{name}” has no maximum speed – CAM then does not limit the spindle speed. Enter the machine's speed and hand it over again.
dialog.uebergeben.tooltip: Saves the machine so that CAM offers it when setting up a job. Repeating overwrites the earlier handover.
uebergeben.trotz_hinweisen:
There are still {anzahl} notes on this machine. Hand it over to CAM anyway?

Missing values then arrive in CAM with default values.
uebergeben.fehler:
The machine could not be saved:
{fehler}
uebergeben.erfolg: The machine “{name}” can now be chosen in CAM.
uebergeben.wo: In CAM: create or edit a job and choose the machine there.
uebergeben.nur_im_dokument: Stored only here in the machine
update.neu:
A new version of the CAM Addon is available: {neu} (installed is {jetzt}).

Update now? Restart FreeCAD afterwards.
update.fertig: Updated. Please restart FreeCAD for the new version to take effect.
update.lokal_geaendert:
Version {neu} of the CAM Addon is available. But the add-on folder contains your own changes – so that nothing gets lost, the add-on does not update itself.

Please update with GitHub Desktop.
update.kein_git:
The CAM Addon cannot look for updates itself: no Git was found on this computer.

Install GitHub Desktop (or Git) and sign in to GitHub once. Until then: update by hand. This note appears only once.
update.fehler: CAM Addon: cannot look for updates ({fehler}).
update.aktuell: You have the latest version of the CAM Addon ({jetzt}).
update.beim_start: Look for updates when FreeCAD starts
update.beim_start.tooltip: Off by default – otherwise every addon checks at start. Checks on GitHub in the background – via Git if the addon was installed with Git (sign-in as in Git or GitHub Desktop), otherwise directly over the internet. You can always check with “Check for updates” in the toolbar.
uebergeben.nicht_verfuegbar:
Your FreeCAD version ({version}) has no machine definition in CAM yet – the machine cannot be handed over there yet.

This works with the FreeCAD weekly build and from the next FreeCAD version on. Your machine stays fully stored here; with a suitable version one click will do.
dialog.uebergeben.tooltip_fehlt: Needs the CAM machine definition – available in the weekly build and from the next FreeCAD version on.
befehl.werkzeugverwaltung.tooltip: Manage tools with their cutting data per material and use case.
wv.werkstoff.tooltip: The material being cut. Just type to search: number, short name, group or old name (e.g. “1.43”, “X5Cr”, “304”, “GG-25”).
wv.alle_werkstoffe.info: What is entered here for a tool applies to every material for which the tool has no values of its own.
wv.neu.tooltip: Adds an end mill with the next free number.
wv.kopieren.tooltip: Adds a copy of the selected tool – with all values and the next free number.
wv.leer: No tools yet. “New” at the bottom left adds the first one – or “Import from CAM” takes them from a FreeCAD tool library.
wv.nummer.tooltip: The tool number (T). Free to choose, each only once.
wv.durchmesser.tooltip: Cutting diameter D. Nothing can be calculated without it.
wv.schneidenlaenge.tooltip: Usable flute length – how deep the tool can cut on its side (largest ap). Empty = unknown.
wv.eckradius.tooltip: Radius at the cutting corner of the bull nose end mill.
wv.schneidstoff.tooltip: What the cutting edge is made of.
wv.bezeichnung.tooltip: Free text to find it again: manufacturer, order number, coating …
wv.hinweis.durchmesser: The diameter is missing – nothing can be calculated without it.
wv.hinweis.nummer: T{nummer} is already taken: {werkzeug}. Each number only once.
wv.frage.speichern: Save the changes in the tool manager?
wv.fehler.speichern:
The tool manager could not be saved:
{fehler}
wv.fehler.laden:
The tool manager file could not be read ({fehler}).

It has been set aside as
{datei}
so nothing is lost. The tool manager starts empty.
wv.schnittwerte.alle: Values for all materials – they apply to every material for which this tool has no values of its own.
wv.schnittwerte.geerbt: For {werkstoff} the values for all materials apply (grey). To change them, add own values – or choose “All materials” at the top.
wv.eigene_anlegen.tooltip: Adds a table of its own for this material – as a copy of the values for all materials.
wv.eigene_loeschen.tooltip: Deletes the own values for this material; the values for all materials apply again.
wv.eigene_loeschen.frage: Delete the own values for {werkstoff}? The values for all materials will apply again.
wv.einsatz.plus.tooltip: New row: ae and ap are prefilled from the diameter, you enter vc and fz from the catalogue. Or a copy of the selected row – for a variant.
wv.spalte.einsatz.tooltip: How the tool works. The name can be changed (double-click).
wv.spalte.ae.tooltip: ae – radial depth of cut (width) in {e_laenge}. Full slot: ae = diameter.
wv.spalte.ap.tooltip: ap – axial depth of cut along the tool axis in {e_laenge}.
wv.spalte.vc.tooltip: vc – cutting speed in {e_schnitt}, from the manufacturer's catalogue.
wv.spalte.fz.tooltip: fz – feed per tooth in {e_span}, from the manufacturer's catalogue.
wv.spalte.f.tooltip: f – feed per revolution in {e_span}, from the manufacturer's catalogue.
wv.spalte.n.tooltip: n – spindle speed in rpm, calculated: n = vc / (π · D).
wv.spalte.vf.tooltip: vf – feed rate in {e_vorschub}, calculated: n · z · fz.
wv.spalte.q.tooltip: Q – metal removal rate in {e_abtrag}, calculated: ae · ap · vf. That much material is gone per minute.
wv.hinweis.ae_zu_gross: ae is larger than the diameter – more than a full slot is not possible.
wv.hinweis.ap_zu_gross: ap {ap} {e_laenge} is longer than the flutes ({laenge} {e_laenge}).
wv.hinweis.vc_fz_fehlen: vc and fz are still missing – they are in the manufacturer's catalogue.
wv.eingriff.bild.tooltip: Left, from above: cutter (blue), material (grey), in red the arc over which each tooth is in the material; feed upwards. Right, from the side: in red the part of the flutes that works at this ap.
wv.eingriff.winkel: Engagement {winkel}° – each tooth is in the material for {anteil} % of the revolution.
wv.ausgleich.tooltip: With ae below D/2 the chip gets thinner than fz. Enter the chip thickness you want – usually the fz from the catalogue – and the addon calculates the fz that gives it.
wv.ausgleich.knopf.tooltip: Sets fz in the selected row to the calculated value.
wv.hinweis.span_duenn: The chip is only {h} {e_span} thick – the edge rubs more than it cuts. Increase fz (chip thinning).
wv.strategie.knopf.tooltip: Two use cases side by side: removal rate, time, wear – with a verdict in sentences.
wv.strategie.q.tooltip: Metal removal rate: that much material is gone per minute. More is faster.
wv.strategie.zeit.tooltip: How long it takes to remove {vergleichsvolumen} {e_volumen} – the same as Q, just tangible.
wv.strategie.weg.tooltip: How far every point of the cutting edge travels through the material to remove 1 {e_volumen}. Less means less wear – a rule of thumb at the same vc.
wv.strategie.ap.tooltip: How much of the flute length is working (ap). The wear is spread over that much of the edge.
wv.strategie.eingriff.tooltip: Which part of a revolution each tooth spends in the material; it cools down for the rest. Full slot: 50 %.
wv.strategie.span.tooltip: How thick the chip gets at most. Too thin: the edge rubs. Too thick: it chips.
wv.strategie.leistung.tooltip: Roughly calculated from the material's kc1.1, without machine efficiency; plus the torque at the spindle. Only if the material has a kc1.1 value.
wv.urteil.unvollstaendig: Values are still missing for a verdict: both use cases need ae, ap, vc and fz.
wv.urteil.q_gleich: Both remove about the same amount per minute.
wv.urteil.q: {schnell} removes {faktor} times as much per minute as {langsam}.
wv.urteil.weg_weniger: Every point of the cutting edge travels {faktor} times less through the material with {schnell} – correspondingly less wear per {e_volumen}.
wv.urteil.weg_mehr: In return, every point of the cutting edge travels {faktor} times as far through the material with {schnell} – more wear per {e_volumen}.
wv.urteil.ap: The wear is spread over {ap_viel} {e_laenge} instead of {ap_wenig} {e_laenge} of the edge.
wv.urteil.eingriff: With {name} each tooth is in the material for only {anteil_wenig} % instead of {anteil_viel} % of the revolution – it cools down for the rest.
wv.urteil.leistung: {name} needs about {leistung} kW of cutting power, the other use case {andere} kW (without efficiency) – does that suit the spindle?
wv.urteil.span_duenn: With {name} the chip is only {h} {e_span} thick – the edge rubs rather than cuts.
wv.werkstoffe.tooltip: The whole material list – with search, all data and your own materials.
ws.suche.platzhalter: Search: number, short name, group, old name …
ws.nichts_gefunden: Nothing found – search differently or add your own with “New…”.
ws.info.eigen: Own material: “Edit…” or a double-click changes it.
ws.info.mitgeliefert: Supplied and read-only. “Copy as own” makes an editable copy.
ws.kopieren.tooltip: Turns the selected material into an own, editable one – with all its data.
ws.bearbeiten.tooltip: Changes the selected own material (also by double-click).
ws.loeschen.tooltip: Deletes the selected own material (asks first).
ws.loeschen.schnittwerte: Tools with own cutting data for this material: {anzahl}. That data is deleted as well.
ws.feld.nummer.platzhalter: e.g. 1.4301 – empty if there is none
ws.feld.kc.tooltip: Reference values for the cutting force, from a handbook. Only for the power in the strategy comparison; empty = unknown.
ws.hinweis.kurzname: The short name is missing – it is how the material is recognised.
wv.cam: Save and hand over to CAM
wv.cam.tooltip: Saves and writes all tools as the tool library “CAM-Addon” into FreeCAD CAM – in the weekly build with the cutting data as suggestions.
wv.cam.werkzeuge: Handed over: {anzahl} – the tools are now in CAM, in the tool library “CAM-Addon”.
wv.cam.presets: Cutting data suggestions with them: {anzahl}. In a job's tool controller, the feeds and speeds button (“Feeds and Speeds Wizard”) suggests them – matching the stock material and the operation.
wv.cam.ohne_werkstoff: For these materials FreeCAD has no material card with the same number – there the suggestion only applies if the stock has a material with the same name: {liste}.
wv.cam.ohne_presets: This FreeCAD version does not yet take the cutting data onto the tools – the weekly build and the next version do. The tools themselves are there.
wv.cam.ohne_durchmesser: Not handed over because the diameter is missing: {anzahl}.
wv.cam.entfernt: Removed from CAM because they no longer exist here: {anzahl}.
wv.cam.weiter: Next: the quickest way is “Cutting data into the job” → “Add tool controller”, which creates the tool controllers with speed and feed in one step. By hand: in a CAM job, add a tool and choose the library “CAM-Addon”. Where overall length or shank are empty, they are estimated (flute length + 2 × D, shank = D).
wv.cam.fehler:
Handing over to CAM did not work:
{fehler}
befehl.schnittwerte_job.tooltip: Sets spindle speed and feed of a CAM job's tool controllers from the tool manager – matching the stock material.
sj.werkstoff.tooltip: The material whose cutting data applies. Preselected is the stock material, if the tool manager knows it.
sj.herkunft.unbekannt: The stock has no material the tool manager knows – the values for all materials apply. You can choose one above.
sj.kein_werkzeug.tooltip: This tool does not come from the library “CAM-Addon”, and no tool in the tool manager has the same T number and diameter. Remedy: in the tool manager, “Import from CAM” – then number and diameter match – and enter use cases there; or “Add tool controller” here.
sj.hinweis: Spindle speed, feed rate and plunge feed are set (a third of the feed rate, the full one for drilling). Use cases without vc and fz are not suggested.
sj.gesetzt: Tool controllers set: {anzahl}. Ctrl+Z undoes it in one step.
sp.knopf.tooltip: Works out how much material this cutter removes using the full flute length and a narrow ae – limited by tool and machine – and adds the result as a use case.
sp.knopf.nicht_moeglich: Only for flat and bull nose end mills with diameter and number of flutes.
sp.erklaerung: This removes the most material: use the full flute length (large ap), step over narrowly (small ae) and raise fz until the chip is as thick as wanted anyway. The planner works this out for every width and suggests the one with the highest removal rate that tool and machine allow.
sp.vc.tooltip: From the manufacturer's catalogue. With a small engagement many manufacturers allow more than for slotting – look it up there.
sp.spandicke.tooltip: The largest chip thickness each tooth should cut. Taken from the selected row – for a full slot it equals fz. With a narrow ae the planner raises fz until this thickness is kept.
sp.ap.tooltip: How much of the flute length cuts. Default: the flute length, at most 2 × D.
sp.ae_grenze.tooltip: From this width on, rows turn red – you can still pick them. Default: 10 % of D at full flute length, however many flutes. Manufacturers usually state 5 to 15 % – more in aluminium, less in stainless steel, titanium and hardened steel. Applies to this tool and is saved with it. Empty: no warning limit.
sp.drehzahl.tooltip: The highest spindle speed. If vc needs more, the planner uses this speed and says which vc results.
sp.vorschub.tooltip: The highest cutting feed of the machine (not the rapid). With a very narrow ae, fz gets large – then the feed limits and the chip gets thinner.
sp.leistung.tooltip: Rated spindle power. 80 % of it is assumed to reach the cutting edge. This needs a kc1.1 value for the material.
sp.von_maschine.tooltip: Takes the maximum speed and feed of a machine from an open document – described with “Edit machine”.
sp.spalte.prozent.tooltip: ae as a percentage of the diameter.
sp.spalte.fz.tooltip: fz – raised so that the chip has the wanted thickness (chip thinning compensation).
sp.spalte.leistung.tooltip: Cutting power at the edge in kW – rough, from the material's kc1.1 value.
sp.drehzahl_ergebnis: Speed {n} rpm – the same for all rows, since vc and D stay the same.
sp.drehzahl_begrenzt: Speed {n} rpm – the machine can't go faster. vc drops to {vc} {e_schnitt}.
sp.hinweis.ueber_ae: more than your warning limit ({grenze} % of D)
sp.hinweis.vorschub: feed at its limit, chip only {h} {e_span}
sp.hinweis.span_duenn: chip too thin – the edge rubs
sp.fehlt: Values are missing for the plan: enter vc, chip thickness and ap.
sp.vorschlag: Suggestion: ae {ae} {e_laenge} ({prozent} % of D), ap {ap} {e_laenge}, fz {fz} {e_span} at vc {vc} {e_schnitt} – that gives {vf} {e_vorschub} and {q} {e_abtrag}.
sp.grund.ae: Wider goes beyond your warning limit of {grenze} % of D – you can still pick the red rows.
sp.grund.leistung: Wider, the spindle power isn't enough ({leistung} kW, 80 % of it at the edge).
sp.grund.ende: Wider than D/2 is no longer dynamic milling.
sp.kein_vorschlag: No suggestion: even at ae = {ae} {e_laenge} it takes more than the {leistung} kW of the spindle. Enter less ap or a smaller chip thickness.
sp.vorschub_begrenzt: The machine's feed limits: the chip is only {h} {e_span} thick.
sp.leistung_unbekannt: The planner only checks the spindle power if the material has a kc1.1 value – select such a material above or enter the value under “Materials…”.
sp.uebernehmen.tooltip: Adds the selected row as “Dynamic roughing” to the table – if the material has no values of its own yet, they are created for it.
sj.zustellung: Also set step over (ae) and step down (ap) of the matching operations
sj.zustellung.tooltip: The operations that use the tool controller get ae as step over (in % of D, rounded down) and ap as step down – but only if the use case fits: Adaptive gets “Dynamic roughing” and “Roughing”, Pocket Shape “Roughing”, Face “Face milling” and “Roughing”, Slot “Full slot”. A Profile gets nothing – it is also used for cutting out, in a full slot.
sj.gesetzt.operationen: Tool controllers set: {anzahl}, plus step over and step down in: {operationen}. Ctrl+Z undoes it in one step.
wv.gesamtlaenge.tooltip: Length of the whole tool – only for CAM (simulation, collision). Empty: estimated as flute length + 2 × D.
wv.schaft.tooltip: Diameter of the shank – only for CAM. Empty: same as the diameter.
wv.hinweis.gesamtlaenge: The overall length ({laenge} {e_laenge}) is shorter than the flutes ({schneide} {e_laenge}).
sj.tc_neu.tooltip: Adds a tool controller for a tool of the tool manager to the job – named after the use case (“T3 Dynamic roughing”), with spindle speed and feed. The tools are handed over to CAM first.
sj.tc_neu.leer: No tool with vc and fz
sj.tc_neu.fehler:
The tool controller could not be added:
{fehler}
wv.aus_cam.tooltip: Takes the tools of a FreeCAD CAM tool library – type, T number, dimensions and tool material. You then enter the cutting data here. Saved with OK or Apply.
wv.aus_cam.leer: No tool library in FreeCAD CAM
wv.aus_cam.fehler:
The tools could not be imported:
{fehler}
wv.aus_cam.bericht.neue_nummer: With a new number, because the old one is already taken here: {liste}.
wv.aus_cam.bericht.andere_form: Not imported – the tool manager doesn't know these shapes: {namen}.
wv.aus_cam.bericht.weiter: Now enter the use cases with vc and fz from the catalogue for each tool. Saved with OK or Apply.
befehl.verfahren.tooltip: Moves the machine's axes by hand – one slider per axis, the assembly moves along.
vf.erklaerung: One slider per axis: drag it or type a value, the machine moves along. It doesn't go beyond the joint's limits. OK keeps the position, Cancel moves everything back.
vf.keine_achsen: This assembly has no axis that can be moved: no slider or revolute joint connected to the fixed part through other parts.
vf.regler.tooltip: Drag to move the axis. With the arrow keys in small steps.
vf.grundstellung.tooltip: Moves all axes to the position they had when the window was opened.
vf.grenzen.tooltip: The limits are set in the assembly's joint (minimum/maximum length or angle) – that is where they can be entered or changed.
vf.platz.tooltip: Choose a turret station: the turret turns until this station is where P1 was when the window opened.
wv.suche.tooltip: Shows only the tools whose row or description contains every word.
sj.am_rohteil.tooltip: Sets the selected material as a FreeCAD material card on the job's stock (same material number). Then this dialog suggests it by itself next time – and in the weekly build FreeCAD's own feeds and speeds button does too. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
wv.werkzeugbild.tooltip: The tool in the right proportions: shank, flutes and tip. Dashed is what is estimated because the field is empty.
sp.vergleich: For comparison: {name} (ae {ae} {e_laenge}, ap {ap_vollnut} {e_laenge}) removes {q_vollnut} {e_abtrag} – the suggestion {faktor} times as much, with {ap} instead of {ap_vollnut} {e_laenge} of edge.
wv.strategie.alle: All use cases of this table
wv.strategie.alle.tooltip: One use case per row; bold is the best per column (most removal, least time and edge travel, most edge used). A click takes the row as B.
wv.umrechnen.frage: The diameter changes from {alt} to {neu} {e_laenge}. Should ae and ap of all use cases be converted as well – in the same ratio, for all materials? vc and fz stay, they come from the catalogue.
wv.eintauchwinkel.tooltip: How steeply the cutter may plunge at most – on a ramp or helix. Stated in the manufacturer's catalogue. “Cutting data into the job” sets it as the helix entry angle in Adaptive. Empty: FreeCAD's default.
sj.ebene_duenn: {operation}: the last level is only {rest} {e_laenge} thick – a pass of its own for little material. Levels count from the top of the stock, and by default FreeCAD puts it 1 mm above the model (in the job: Stock, the right field of “Ext. Z”).
sj.ebene_duenn.ap: With ap {ap} {e_laenge} in the use case it goes away – the flute is {laenge} {e_laenge} long.
wv.aus_cam.bericht.unlesbar: Could not be read – what FreeCAD reports about it is in the Report view: {namen}.
wv.name: Name
wv.name.tooltip: The tool's name in the control (e.g. T="Endmill carbide 12") – write it exactly as on the machine. Empty: the name shown in grey, made from the data, applies. CAM names the tool like this.
wv.zeile.name: T{nummer}  {name} · {art} {werte}
wv.hinweis.name: “{name}” is also the name of T{nummer} – intended (sister tool)?
wv.beispiel: Grey: example values – they apply until you enter your own.
sp.beispiel: Grey: example for steel with {schneidstoff} – the table already uses it. Better use the values from your tool's catalogue.
dialog.beispielmaschine.tooltip: Builds a ready-made machine in a new document – a lathe or 3-axis mill with your dimensions, 5-axis mills – and opens it right here.
sp.warnung.ueber_ae: Selected: ae {ae} {e_laenge}, {prozent} % of D – more than your warning limit of {grenze} % of D. You can take it over; the tool is loaded more than you planned, though.
wv.zustellung.tooltip: How ae and ap are shown in the table: in mm or in percent of the diameter (ap 25 mm at Ø 12 = 208 %). They are always saved in mm; the choice applies to all tools and is kept for next time.
wv.spitzenwinkel.tooltip: Angle at the tip, measured across both cutting edges: twist drills usually 118° (for steel and stainless steel also 130° or 140°), spot drills 90° or 120°, center drills 60°, chamfer mills and countersinks 90°. Empty: the usual angle of the type (grey in the field). Goes to CAM and into the picture.
zahlen.frage: And how should numbers look – unit system and decimal separator?
einstellungen.zahlen.hinweis: Applies to all dialogs of the addon as soon as they are opened again. Values are always saved in metric. You can always type either, a point or a comma.
zahlen.metrisch: Millimetres: Ø 12 mm · vc 120 m/min · vf 800 mm/min
zahlen.zoll: Inch: Ø 1 in · vc 400 SFM · vf 30 ipm
wv.masssystem.tooltip: Unit system: mm or inch. Applies right away to the whole addon – fields, tables, planner; values are always saved in mm. Also under Edit → Preferences → CAM Addon.
befehl.update.tooltip: Checks on GitHub whether there is a new version of the CAM Addon and offers to update. The addon doesn't check by itself – that can be switched on under Edit → Preferences → CAM Addon.
wv.spitzen_d.tooltip: Diameter at the tip: for chamfer mills and countersinks the smallest point of the cutting edge (0 = pointed), for corner rounding cutters and counterbores the pilot below.
wv.kegelwinkel.tooltip: How steep the cutting edge stands against the axis, per side – as in the catalogue ("3° per side"). CAM gets the full taper angle, i.e. twice this.
wv.flankenwinkel.tooltip: Angle between the flanks: metric and inch threads 60° (Whitworth 55°), dovetails mostly 60° or 45°. Empty: the usual angle of the type (grey in the field).
wv.hals_d.tooltip: Diameter of the neck between cutting edge and shank – smaller than the cutting edge so that it cuts freely.
wv.hals_laenge.tooltip: Length of the neck – how deep the tool reaches behind the cutting edge without hitting.
wv.profilradius.tooltip: The radius the corner rounding cutter mills onto the edge.
wv.steigung.tooltip: Pitch of the thread – the distance per revolution (M10: 1.5 mm). In inch as threads per inch (1/2"-13 UNC: 13).
wv.schneidenbreite.tooltip: Width of the cutting edge – how wide the slot or groove gets in one pass.
wv.einstellwinkel.tooltip: Angle between cutting edge and feed direction (κ): face mills mostly 45° or 90°, turning tools often 93° or 95°. Empty: the usual angle of the type (grey in the field).
wv.plattenwinkel.tooltip: Nose angle of the insert (ε): C and W 80°, D 55°, V 35°, T 60°, S 90°. Empty: 80° (C insert).
wv.stechtiefe.tooltip: How deep the grooving tool can cut at most.
wv.ausfuehrung.tooltip: Right, left or neutral – how the holder carries the cutting edge.
wv.hinweis.steigung: The pitch is missing – without it the feed of the tap cannot be calculated.
wv.cam.ohne_form: Not handed over – FreeCAD CAM does not turn, so turning tools stay here: {liste}.
wv.ohne_schnittwerte.drehen: Turning tools have no cutting data here yet: FreeCAD CAM does not turn. Dimensions and picture are there anyway – as soon as FreeCAD can turn, vc, f and ap will follow.
wv.ohne_schnittwerte.taster: A probe does not cut – it has no cutting data.
wv.hinweis.vc_fehlt: vc is still missing – it is in the manufacturer's catalogue. The add-on calculates the feed from the pitch.
wv.cam.naeherung: CAM has no shape of its own for these types – they are there as the closest one: {liste}.
beispiel.drehmaschine.beschreibung: Slant bed like a CLX. Main spindle S1/C1 – its axis is Z –, X, Y, Z and a turret T. Every station is a VDI mount on the tool drive S3 – in the face of the disc or on its circumference; how a tool stands is up to its holder in the tool manager. Enter bed slant, X in diameter or radius, travels, stations, turret and an inclined Y axis below.
beispiel.fraese3.beschreibung: Cross table X/Y, milling head Z, spindle S1 – the simplest start. Two clamps on the table as an example – move or delete them in the tree.
beispiel.tisch_tisch.beschreibung: Trunnion: the cradle tilts about A (about X), on it the rotary table turns about C. X, Y and Z move the head (travelling column).
beispiel.kopf_kopf.beschreibung: Gantry machine with a fork head: A tilts about X, inside it B about Y. The table stands still – all five axes are in the head.
beispiel.kopf_tisch.beschreibung: The swivel head tilts about B (about Y), the rotary table in the machine table turns about C. X, Y and Z move the head.
beispiel.auswahl.text: Which machine? It comes ready-made in a new document – with axes, spindles and mounts. For the lathe and the 3-axis mill, the main dimensions can be entered.
eigenschaft.transformation: Which conversion of the control this is – so far there is only the inclined axis.
eigenschaft.schraeg: The axis whose slide moves at an angle – usually Y1. For a Y in the program it moves together with the compensating axis.
eigenschaft.ausgleich: The axis that moves along so the tool travels square – usually X1. A pure X in the program moves only this one.
eigenschaft.name_schraeg: What the inclined axis is called in the NC program – usually Y.
eigenschaft.name_ausgleich: What the compensating axis is called in the NC program – usually X.
maschine.trafo_achse_fehlt: The inclined axis “{name}” is missing an axis – choose the inclined and the compensating axis in the entry.
maschine.trafo_gleiche_achse: In the inclined axis “{name}”, “{achse}” is both inclined and compensating – these must be two different axes.
maschine.trafo_nicht_linear: The inclined axis “{name}” needs two linear axes – “{achse}” is not one.
maschine.trafo_parallel: {schraeg} and {ausgleich} move in (almost) the same direction – no square “{name}” can be computed from them. The angle must be between −89° and 89°.
dialog.transformationen.tooltip: Conversions done by the control: the program is square, the slides move differently – for example with an inclined Y axis, where both slides move for Y.
dialog.schraege_achse_neu.tooltip: One slide moves at an angle to another, and the control converts a square Y onto both (Siemens TRAANG). For a Y in the program, both slides then move.
dialog.schraege_achse_neu.fehlt: This needs two linear axes – joints with the operating mode Linear.
dialog.keine_transformation: none – only needed if the control converts
dialog.detail_schraege_achse: Inclined axis – for {name} in the program, {schraeg} and {ausgleich} move together
dialog.winkel.tooltip: How far {schraeg} is tilted out of the right angle to {ausgleich} – measured at the joints of the assembly. 0° means square; positive when {schraeg} leans towards the plus side of {ausgleich} – as in the picture. If you enter a different angle, the guideway of {schraeg} turns along in the assembly; the slide and everything on it stay where they are.
dialog.beispiel_schraeg.tooltip: This is how the control converts: for a move in just this direction of the program, both slides move.
dialog.winkel_zu_gross: At most ±89° – at 90° both slides would move in the same direction, and there would be no “{name}” left.
maschine.trafo_schraeg_erkannt: {schraeg} is tilted {winkel} out of square with {ausgleich}. Does the control convert a square “{name}” onto both (inclined axis, Siemens TRAANG)? Clicking this note adds it under “Transformations”.
vf.modus.programm.tooltip: The axes as in the NC program: square. For {name}, {schraeg} and {ausgleich} move together – this is how the control converts with the inclined axis.
vf.modus.maschine.tooltip: One slider per slide – as when setting up by hand.
vf.programmachse.tooltip: Axis of the program – the control converts it onto {schraeg} and {ausgleich}.
vf.grenzen_programm: At most {min} … {max} {einheit} – how far it goes depends on where {andere} is.
vf.anschlag: {name} cannot go further here: {achse} is at its limit {grenze}.
export.schraege_achse: “{name}” is an inclined axis ({winkel} to {ausgleich}). CAM gets it square, like “{programm}” in the program, with converted limits and rapid rate. These limits only hold while {ausgleich} has room to compensate – how far it really goes is shown by “Move machine” as in the program.
befehl.neue_maschine.tooltip: Builds a ready-made machine in a new document – lathe and 3-axis mill with your dimensions: travels, speed, for the lathe also bed slant, inclined Y axis, turret stations.
neu.masse.fest: This type has fixed dimensions – for trying things out. After building, everything can be changed in the assembly.
neu.name: Name:
neu.name.tooltip: Name of the machine and the document. Empty: the name of the type.
neu.bettneigung.tooltip: How steeply the bed rises towards the back – 0° is a flat bed, 30°, 45° or 60° are common. X travels on the bed, so it is slanted the same way.
neu.y_winkel.tooltip: 0° means: the Y slide moves at right angles to X. Otherwise it is inclined by that much, and the control converts a square Y onto both slides – the addon adds the inclined axis right away.
neu.x.tooltip: How your control shows X and expects it in the program – in diameter on almost every lathe. The X travel below counts the same way. The machine remembers it, and the post processor writes X accordingly.
neu.weg.tooltip: From … to, counted from the position in which the machine is built – 0 lies in between. These become the limits of the joint.
neu.plaetze.tooltip: The addon distributes this many stations in a circle on the turret disc (P1 … Pn).
neu.revolver.umfang: VDI on the circumference (radial, star turret)
neu.revolver.tooltip: Where the VDI mounts sit. In the face: the holders go into the disc along Z – a straight holder drills along Z, an angled one (“VDI30 driven radial”) mills radially. On the circumference (star turret): the holders go in radially – a straight holder stands radial to the spindle axis, an angle head mills along Z.
neu.scheibe.tooltip: Diameter of the turret disc. Mounts in the face lie 40 mm inside the edge, those on the circumference on the edge.
neu.vdi.tooltip: Shank Ø of the holders (VDI 20 … 60) – the size of the ring around each mount. Choose the holders themselves to match in the tool manager.
neu.revolver_unbekannt: This turret type does not exist.
neu.scheibe_bereich: The turret disc needs 240 to 600 mm Ø.
neu.vdi_unbekannt: This VDI size does not exist: 20, 25, 30, 40, 50 or 60.
neu.drehzahl.tooltip: The maximum speed of main spindle S1 – on the mill, of spindle S1.
neu.drehzahl.werkzeuge.tooltip: The maximum speed of the driven tools in the turret (tool drive S3) – often less than the main spindle's. “Plan roughing values” takes this one from the machine.
neu.bettneigung_bereich: The bed slant must be between 0° and 60°.
neu.y_winkel_bereich: Y may be inclined by at most 60°.
neu.weg_bereich: Every travel needs some length: from at most 0 to at least 0, not both 0.
neu.weg_leer: Every travel needs a length: “to” must be greater than “from”.
neu.wege.drehmaschine: Counted as on the machine, up to the centre of the VDI mount: X from the spindle axis (as chosen under “X as”), Z from the spindle nose.
neu.weg_x.drehmaschine.tooltip: From … to: where the centre of the VDI mount in working position is, from the spindle axis – in diameter (twice the distance) or as a radius, as chosen under “X as”. 0: it is on the spindle axis – a drill drills into the centre of the part there; negative: past the centre.
neu.weg_y.drehmaschine.tooltip: From … to, from the spindle centre: 0 means the centre of the VDI mount is level with the spindle axis.
neu.weg_z.drehmaschine.tooltip: From … to: the distance of the face of the VDI mount (where the holders sit) from the spindle nose, along the spindle axis.
neu.drehzahl_werkzeuge_fehlt: The maximum speed of the driven tools is missing.
befehl.vierachs.tooltip: Places a part with one of its end faces at the front of a round bar, centred, and sets up a CAM job for it – for rotary axis A, B or C. With “All-round roughing” or its job selected, it opens it for changing.
va.kopf: Step 1 of 2: part into the bar
va.anleitung: In the 3D view, click the flat face of the part that should sit at the front of the bar.
va.nicht_eben: {flaeche} of “{teil}” is not flat – only a flat face can sit at the front of the bar. Click a flat end face.
va.stange.tooltip: Diameter of the round bar. Left empty, the grey suggestion applies: the next 5 mm step (1/8" in inch) that leaves at least 1 mm all round.
va.mitte.teil: whole part as central as possible
va.mitte.tooltip: What sits on the bar axis: the centre of the chosen face – or the position in which the whole part fits the thinnest bar. Next to it: the Ø the bar needs for that.
va.drehlage.tooltip: Turns the part in the bar about the bar axis – this sets where 0° of the rotary axis is.
va.planaufmass.tooltip: How far the bar sticks out in front of the part – facing removes it later.
va.abstechbreite.tooltip: Room behind the part for parting off or sawing.
va.spannlaenge.tooltip: How far the bar sits in the chuck.
va.rundachse.tooltip: The axis the bar turns about together with the part. With a machine, it sets the axis – so the bar sits in the chuck as it is clamped when you check the job. Without a machine: A lies along X, B along Y, C along Z.
va.achse.a: A – bar along X, tool from above
va.achse.b: B – bar along Y, tool from above
va.achse.c: C – bar along Z, tool from X, like on a lathe
va.maschine.tooltip: The machine you mill on: it sets the rotary axis – the bar lies along it, as it sits in the chuck. “Check on machine” uses the same one later.
va.maschine.ohne_rundachse: {name} – no rotary axis for the bar
va.maschine.kann: Linear axes {linear} · rotary axis for the bar: {rund} · {plaetze} tool stations
va.maschine.ohne.text: Without a machine you choose the rotary axis yourself: A lies along X, B along Y, C along Z. “Check on machine” needs a machine.
va.maschine.oeffnen_fehler: The machine could not be opened: {fehler}
va.achse.der_maschine_schraeg: {buchstabe} – bar at an angle in the job
va.passt: ✔ Fits – at least {aufmass} {e_laenge} of stock all round.
va.passt_nicht: ✘ Does not fit: the part needs Ø {noetig} {e_laenge} – a bar of Ø {vorschlag} {e_laenge}, say.
va.anlegen.tooltip: Creates job and bar and – with “All-round roughing” and “All-round finishing” – tool controllers and operations. Ctrl+Z first undoes controllers and operations, a second one job and bar.
va.kein_dokument: First open the document with the part that goes into the bar.
va.fehler: The job could not be created: {fehler}
rw.ueberschreitung: {achse} travels to {stellung} in “{operation}”; the limit is {grenze} (at {punkt}).
rw.ueberschreitung.spitze: At the limit the tip of {werkzeug} would be at {punkt}.
rw.eigenschaft: Job origin as seen from the workpiece mount (CAM Addon, “Check on machine”)
rw.keine_werkstueckaufnahme: The machine has no workpiece mount with an LCS – without one the check cannot tell where the job sits.
rw.keine_werkzeugaufnahme: The machine has no tool mount with an LCS – without one the check cannot tell where the tool sits.
rw.laenge_gesamt: {werkzeug}: calculated with the overall length {laenge} – without holder. More exact with the “Gauge length” in the tool manager.
rw.laenge_geschaetzt: {werkzeug}: no overall length entered – calculated with an estimated {laenge}, without holder. More exact with the “Gauge length” in the tool manager.
rw.laenge_cam: {werkzeug}: calculated with the length of the CAM tool, {laenge} – without holder. The tool is not in the tool manager, which would have the “Gauge length”.
rw.platz_fehlt: “{operation}”: turret {revolver} has no station P{nummer} for T{nummer} – skipped.
rw.bestueckung.frei_nirgends: In “{operation}” the job calls T{nummer} – {platz} is free according to the loading, and {werkzeug} is in no station. Load it under “Tool loading” in “Edit machine”.
rw.bestueckung.frei_woanders: In “{operation}” the job calls T{nummer} – {platz} is free according to the loading, {werkzeug} is in {richtig}. Set the controller to T{richtig_nummer} or move the tool.
rw.bestueckung.anderes_nirgends: In “{operation}” the job calls T{nummer} – according to the loading {platz} holds {anderes}, not {werkzeug}. Move it under “Tool loading” in “Edit machine”.
rw.bestueckung.anderes_woanders: In “{operation}” the job calls T{nummer} – according to the loading {platz} holds {anderes}; {werkzeug} is in {richtig}. Set the controller to T{richtig_nummer} or move the tool.
rw.z_verkehrt: The Z axis of the tool mount “{aufnahme}” points towards the workpiece. It should point from the tool tip to the mount – otherwise the tip ends up on the wrong side.
rw.zu_viele_achsen: There are more linear axes between tool and workpiece than can be resolved uniquely ({achsen}) – the add-on cannot check this yet.
rw.befehl: “{operation}”: the check does not know the command {befehl} – skipped.
rw.unerreichbar: In “{operation}” the tool cannot reach every point, e.g. at {punkt}: {anzahl} of {gesamt} points lie outside what the linear axes can reach.
befehl.reichweite.tooltip: Checks a CAM job on a machine: do the axes reach far enough, how does the machine run the path, does anything collide on the way?
rw.erklaerung: Checks the job's paths on this machine: verdicts at the top, details below. Close moves the machine back.
rw.maschine.tooltip: The machine the check runs on – the addon remembers it and opens it by itself next time. For another one: close this panel, open the file of the other machine and run the command again; with several open it asks.
rw.nullpunkt: Job origin, as seen from the workpiece mount:
rw.nullpunkt.tooltip: Where the job origin sits on the machine – measured from the LCS of the workpiece mount, along its axes (like G54). Empty fields use the suggestion (grey): the stock centred on the mount, its bottom on the clamping face. The job remembers what you enter.
rw.liste.tooltip: Click to move the machine there – the axis then stops at its limit.
rw.nicht_in_grenzen: Not all axes stay within their limits – where, see below.
rw.in_grenzen: All axes stay within their limits.
rw.keine_punkte: No path to check – the job's operations have no points.
rw.kein_job: There is no CAM job in any open document. Open the document with the job – this command then checks its paths on a machine.
rw.keine_maschine: No machine is open. Open the file with your machine – the addon remembers it for next time. Or create one with “New machine …” – the check then runs on it right away.
wv.laenge_spindelnase.tooltip: From the spindle nose (in a turret: from the tool mount) to the tip, with holder – as the presetter measures it. “Check on machine” uses it to see whether Z reaches. Empty, with a holder: holder length + overall length − clamping depth; without a holder the overall length.
ab.ohne_vorschub: “{operation}” has no feed rate – moved at {vorschub}. The tool controller sets the feed (or “Cutting data into the job”).
ab.operation.tooltip: Jumps to the start of the chosen operation.
ab.anfang.tooltip: To the start of the job
ab.zurueck.tooltip: One point of the path back
ab.vor.tooltip: One point of the path on
ab.tempo.tooltip: How fast: ×1 is as fast as on the machine – without acceleration, so a little too fast.
ab.schieber.tooltip: The time within the job – drag it and the machine follows.
ab.keine_bahn: Nothing to run through: no operation with a path whose tool fits this machine.
ab.nicht_erreichbar: The axes cannot reach this point – the machine stays where it is.
ab.spitze.tooltip: Where the tool tip is right now, in program coordinates (X, Y, Z as in the NC program, plus the rotary axes). The axes above are the machine's slides – with a tool the tip is elsewhere. If an axis is at its stop, red text behind says where the tip should be.
rm.laeuft: The bar is removed while playing; at the last station the comparison with the finished part shows in colours.
rm.ergebnis: At the end {von} … {bis} remain on the part (allowance {aufmass}), nowhere into the part.
rm.ins_teil: At the end up to {bis} remain on the part – in places up to {tief} are missing from the part (blue)!
rm.zu_viel: Red: more than {grenze} left – the cutter did not get there.
rm.nur_gewaehlte: Compared on the selected faces – what is not selected stays bar stock and has no colour.
rm.nicht_rundum: From {stellen} along the axis the part does not lie all around the axis – the simulation does not compare there: it knows only one radius per ray from the axis and would not see what of the part remains behind the cutter.
rm.farben: Green: the allowance, yellow: a little more, red: over 1 mm more, blue: into the part.
ab.hinsehen.tooltip: View the workpiece and tool – the machine is usually much bigger than the part.
ab.bahn.tooltip: Shows the tool path – feed blue, rapid red. Without the tick you see better how the bar is removed while playing; at the end, with the colours, the path is always off.
halter.beispielmasse: Example dimensions – check against the catalogue
hd.neu.tooltip: Add a holder – empty or from a template with example dimensions.
hd.kopieren.tooltip: A copy of the chosen holder, e.g. for another length.
hd.loeschen.tooltip: Delete the chosen holder; tools using it are left without a holder.
hd.loeschen.frage: “{halter}” belongs to {werkzeuge}. Delete anyway? The tools are then without a holder.
hd.leer: No holder yet – “New” adds one, empty or from a template.
hd.name: Name
hd.name.tooltip: How the holder is called in the tool's selection, e.g. “SK40 ER32 A70”.
hd.spanntiefe.tooltip: How deep the tool's shank sits in the holder. The tool manager uses it to estimate the gauge length until someone measures it.
hd.kontur.tooltip: From the spindle nose towards the tool, section by section: equal diameters make a cylinder, different ones a cone. What sits inside the spindle does not count.
hd.abschnitt.dazu.tooltip: Insert a section below the chosen one.
hd.unbenutzt: Not used by any tool yet.
hd.bild.tooltip: The holder in section, the spindle on top; below it the tool down to its tip.
hd.richtung.gerade: straight – the tool in the axis of the mount
hd.richtung.tooltip: How the tool stands to the machine. Straight: in the axis of the spindle or turret station. Angled: tilted by the angle to it – a driven radial holder on the turret, an angle head in the milling spindle.
hd.winkel.tooltip: Between the axis of the mount and the axis of the tool: at 90° it stands at a right angle (radial), at 0° straight. A universal angle head allows any angle.
hd.drehung.tooltip: About the axis of the mount, from its reference direction X: at 0° the tool points there – on the turret towards the spindle axis. Not visible in the picture next to it: that shows the plane of the bend.
hd.versatz.tooltip: From the mount (spindle nose, turret station) along its axis to the axis of the tool. The reference point is there: the contour and the length of the tool run from it.
hd.kopf_d.tooltip: The head from the mount to the bend, as a cylinder – the collision check uses it; it reaches beyond the tool axis by its radius.
hd.kontur.gewinkelt: Contour from the reference point, along the tool axis:
wv.laenge_bezugspunkt.tooltip: The holder is angled: from the reference point – where the tool axis meets the axis of the mount – along the tool axis to the tip, as a presetter measures driven tools. Empty means: holder length + overall length − clamping depth.
wv.halter.tooltip: The holder between spindle nose and tool – for the collision check and the gauge length.
wv.halter.knopf.tooltip: Add and edit holders; with OK this tool gets the chosen one.
rw.laenge_halter: {werkzeug}: calculated with {laenge}, estimated from holder and tool (holder length + overall length − clamping depth). More precise with the measured “gauge length” in the tool manager.
rw.laenge_halter_gewinkelt: {werkzeug}: calculated with {laenge}, estimated from holder and tool (holder outlet + overall length − clamping depth). More precise with the measured “length from reference point” in the tool manager.
kb.beruehrung.eilgang: In “{operation}”, {a} and {b} touch during a rapid move (block {satz}, at {punkt}).
kb.naehe: In “{operation}”, {a} and {b} come within {abstand} of each other (block {satz}, at {punkt}).
kb.naehe.eilgang: In “{operation}”, {a} and {b} come within {abstand} of each other during a rapid move (block {satz}, at {punkt}).
kb.ohne_halter: {werkzeug}: checked without holder – choose the holder with the tool in the tool manager.
kb.schon_beruehrt: {a} and {b} already touch in the home position – the collision check skips this pair.
kb.kein_teil: The job has no model – nothing was checked against the part.
kb.fehler: {a} and {b}: FreeCAD could not compute their distance – this pair is not checked.
kb.zu_viele: Stopped after {anzahl} positions – checked up to {zeit} of {dauer}.
kb.warnabstand.tooltip: If two bodies come closer than this, it shows in yellow; empty means 1 mm.
kb.pruefen.tooltip: Runs through the whole path and looks whether tool, holder or machine bump into anything – the part, the fixtures, the machine. Takes a few seconds depending on the path.
kb.noch_nicht: Not checked yet – “Check for collisions” runs through the path and looks.
kb.abgebrochen.urteil: Cancelled – only the beginning was checked.
kb.nahe: Nothing touches, but some things come closer than {abstand}:
kb.frei: Nothing touches, nothing comes closer than {abstand}.
kb.liste.tooltip: A click sets the player to that spot; a red ball shows it in the view.
sj.kein_job: There is no CAM job in any open document. Open the document with the job – this command then sets the speed and feed of its tool controllers from the tool manager.
update.neu_starten.tooltip: Closes FreeCAD – it asks about unsaved documents first – and starts it again.
jobs.welches_dokument: Several open documents have CAM jobs – which one?
rw.keine_maschine_in_datei: {datei} contains no machine. An assembly becomes a machine with “Edit machine”.
rw.eigenschaft.maschine: File of the machine the job was last checked on (CAM Addon, “Check on machine”)
rw.maschine_oeffnen.tooltip: Open a saved machine (FCStd file). The addon remembers it and opens it by itself the next time you check.
rw.neue_maschine.tooltip: Builds a ready-made machine in a new document – a lathe or 3-axis mill with your dimensions, 5-axis mills – and checks on it right away.
rw.laenge.gemessen: Measured for all tools – from the tool manager.
kb.kurz.nahe: Nothing touches, but some things come closer than {abstand}
dialog.vorschlagen.tooltip: Gives every joint without an operating mode one: sliders linear, the NC name from the joint's name (“X slide” → X1) or from its direction; revolute joints with “spindle” in the name a spindle (S1), with “turret” the turret (T), otherwise positioning (A, B or C by the axis of rotation). You enter the values afterwards – the notes say which are missing.
sj.unbenutzt: Used by no operation and not from the tool manager: {namen}.
sj.unbenutzt.entfernen.tooltip: Removes these tool controllers together with their tool from the job – like deleting them in the tree. Ctrl+Z brings them back.
sj.unbenutzt.tooltip: Such tool controllers do nothing. FreeCAD adds “TC: 5mm Endmill” to every new job – if you work with tools from the tool manager, you do not need it.
wv.schnittwerte.noch_keine: This tool has no cutting data yet. “+ Use case” adds the first one – it applies to all materials.
wv.einsatz.erster_fuer_alle: The first use case applies to all materials – that is why “All materials” is selected at the top now. If the values for {werkstoff} differ, add own values there afterwards.
sj.ebene_duenn.wv_offen: The tool manager is open – change ap there, or close it first. Otherwise its OK would write the old value back.
sj.eigenschaft.einsatz: Use case and material the CAM Addon last set spindle speed and feed from (“Cutting data into the job”)
sj.herkunft.rohteil_gemerkt: From the job's stock, as last time: {werkstoff}.
sj.herkunft.gemerkt: The stock has no material the tool manager knows – preselected is the one from last time: {werkstoff}.
rw.schnittwerte.passen: Spindle speed and feed as in the tool manager.
rw.schnittwerte.veraltet: {tc}: {jetzt} in the job, {neu} per the tool manager
rw.schnittwerte.tooltip: Compared with what “Cutting data into the job” would set: with the use case and material from last time, otherwise the suggestion. “apply” sets the controller's spindle speed and feed – one undo step; the operations' step-over and step-down stay.
rw.rundachse_fehlt: “{operation}” turns about {buchstabe} – the machine has no rotary axis {buchstabe}. The check ignores this rotation.
rw.rundachse_fehlt_andere: “{operation}” turns about {buchstabe} – the machine has no rotary axis {buchstabe}, only {achsen}. The check ignores this rotation. If the job comes from 4-axis machining, choose the machine's rotary axis there.
va.eigenschaft.spannlaenge: How deep the bar sits in the chuck (CAM Addon, 4-axis machining) – “Check on machine” proposes the origin with it
va.eigenschaft.abstechbreite: Part-off width behind the part (CAM Addon, 4-axis machining) – the gap to the chuck can be larger where the cutter needs room
kb.ins_teil: In “{operation}”, {a} runs into the finished part (block {satz}, at {punkt}) – the tool would cut into the part there.
rw.werkzeug_quer: “{operation}”: the path is calculated for a tool along Z, but {werkzeug} sits across it on {aufnahme} – run like that, it does not fit the part. It fits with a straight holder on a station along Z (axial); all round with a radial tool needs a path of its own (4-axis machining).
vo.name: All-round roughing {werkzeug}
vo.eigenschaft.rundachse: The letter of the rotary axis in the program: A, B or C.
vo.eigenschaft.stangenachse: The bar axis pointing forward (away from the chuck), in the job's axes. It passes through the job origin.
vo.eigenschaft.werkzeugrichtung: Where the tool comes from radially while the rotary axis is at 0 – in the job's axes.
vo.eigenschaft.drehsinn: +1: a positive value of the rotary axis turns the part right-handed about the bar axis – that is how FreeCAD shows the path. −1: the other way.
vo.eigenschaft.quer_auf_null: At the start, move the axis across the bar to 0 (Y with C) so the tool is on centre. Off if the machine has no such axis.
vo.eigenschaft.steigung: Feed per revolution of the spiral, along the bar (ae) – at most the cutter diameter.
vo.eigenschaft.aufmass: Finishing allowance: this much stays all round.
vo.eigenschaft.ueberlauf: Overrun: how far the centre of the cutter runs past the back of the part so that it leaves it completely (suggestion: cutter radius + 0.5 mm).
vo.eigenschaft.abstand_futter: Chuck distance: how far the edge of the cutter – or that of its holder, if it reaches further – stays in front of the clamping face (suggestion 5 mm).
vo.eigenschaft.halter_zum_futter: Holder towards chuck: how far the tool's holder reaches sideways beyond the tool axis – the wizard enters it from the tool manager. If it reaches further than the cutter, the chuck distance counts from its edge; 0: the cutter only.
vo.eigenschaft.sicherheit: Safety distance above and in front of the bar for rapid moves.
vo.eigenschaft.lagen: Number of layers of the path (calculated).
vo.eigenschaft.flaechen: The selected faces of the model (“Face3” …): the cutter only mills where it touches one of them and lifts in between. Empty: all around.
vo.eigenschaft.eintauchwinkel: How steeply the cutter enters the material between selected faces: back and forth along the path until it is down (default 5°).
vo.fehler.stange: The job's stock is not a round bar (cylinder).
vo.fehler.stange_achse: The bar is not on the rotary axis – its axis must run along the bar axis through the job origin.
vo.fehler.vorschub: The tool controller has no feed rate.
vb.fehler.werte: Cutter, step-down and feed per revolution must be greater than 0.
vb.fehler.steigung: The feed per revolution is larger than the cutter – ridges would remain.
vb.fehler.platz: There is no room for the cutter between chuck and part.
vb.fehler.platz_halter: There is no room for the cutter's holder between chuck and part.
vb.hinten_frei: The cutter cannot reach the last {laenge} in front of the chuck – material stays there. A larger part-off width helps.
vb.fehler.schrittweite: Cutter and stepover must be greater than 0.
vb.fehler.schrittweite_gross: The stepover is larger than the cutter – ridges would remain between the passes.
vb.vorstufen: In narrow spots the roughing cutter could not fully reach, finishing first removes material in stages (pre-passes: {stufen}) – each at most {grenze} deep.
vf.fehler.fehlt: The selected faces {namen} no longer exist in the model – select them again in the wizard.
vf.fehler.nicht_erreichbar: None of the selected faces can be reached from outside – they lie under an overhang or across the axis.
va.kopf.bearbeitung: Step 2 of 2: what do you want to do?
va.weiter.tooltip: On to step 2: what you want to do with the bar – rough it all round, say.
va.zurueck.tooltip: Back to step 1: bar, centre, rotary axis.
va.schruppen.tooltip: Creates the operation “All-round roughing”. Unticked, “Create” only creates job and bar.
va.schruppen.text: Removes the bar all round down to the finishing allowance: in layers, with a cutter pointing at the axis from outside while the rotary axis turns.
va.werkstoff.tooltip: Which material the cutting data are for – the stock's if it has one, otherwise the one used last.
va.fraeser.tooltip: A cutter from the tool manager with cutting data: end, torus, ball, slot or face mill.
va.fraeser.keiner: The tool manager has no cutter with cutting data for this material – add one there (“Tool manager …”).
va.werkzeugverwaltung.tooltip: Opens the tool manager. Once you save there, its cutters are available here.
va.flaechen.tooltip: Which faces are milled: without a selection all around – every outer face. Clicking a face of the part adds it, clicking again removes it.
va.flaechen.liste.tooltip: The selected faces: green reachable, yellow partly, red not – a tool pointing from outside at the axis cannot get there. Double-click removes a face.
va.flaechen.rundum: All around – every outer face. To mill single faces only: click them in 3D (clicking again removes them).
va.flaechen.alle: All outer faces selected – all around.
va.flaechen.nur: Only these faces: the cutter mills where it touches one of them; in between it lifts and re-enters safely.
va.flaechen.alle_knopf.tooltip: Selects every face that faces outwards – that is all around.
va.flaeche.quer: across the axis – formed with the neighbouring faces
va.flaeche.fehlt: no longer exists in the part
va.einsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter apply – “Roughing” preselected. It gives spindle speed, feed and the suggestions for step-down and feed per revolution.
va.zustellung.tooltip: How deep each layer cuts, radially (ap). Empty uses the grey suggestion from the use case.
va.steigung.tooltip: How far the spiral advances along the bar per revolution (ae) – at most the cutter diameter. Empty uses the grey suggestion from the use case.
va.aufmass.tooltip: This much stays all round – for finishing.
va.ueberlauf.tooltip: How far the centre of the cutter runs past the back of the part so that it leaves it completely and the rear edge gets finished. Suggestion: cutter radius + 0.5 mm.
va.abstand_futter.tooltip: How far the edge of the cutter stays in front of the chuck's clamping face – or that of its holder, if it reaches further beyond the tool axis. Suggestion 5 mm.
va.sicherheit.tooltip: How far above and in front of the bar the cutter moves in rapid. Suggestion 2 mm.
va.ausspannen: The bar has to stick out {laenge} {einheit} from the chuck: {teile}.
va.lagen.keine: Nothing to rough: the part already fills the bar.
va.radius: In the program X is the radius, not the diameter – on a lathe switch the program header to radius (Siemens DIAMOF). Feed is given as G93 (1 ÷ time).
va.radius_durchmesser: The machine counts X in diameter, and the check window shows it that way. FreeCAD's own post processors still write X as a radius – for those, switch to radius in the program header (Siemens DIAMOF) until the add-on's post processor writes X in diameter. The feed rate follows G93 (1 ÷ time).
va.schlichten.tooltip: Creates the operation “All-round finishing”: after roughing, one spiral on the part.
va.schlichten.text: After roughing, runs one spiral on the part – the tip on the surface plus allowance, calculated with the cutter's shape. The stepover comes from the tool table.
va.schlichtfraeser.tooltip: A cutter from the tool manager with cutting data whose shape the add-on knows: ball, torus, flat, tapered ball, lollipop, chamfer, radius, slitting, face or dovetail mill.
va.schlichteinsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter applies – “Finishing” preselected. It gives speed, feed and the stepover (ae).
va.schlichtfraeser.keiner: The tool manager has no cutter “All-round finishing” can calculate with (with cutting data for this material) – add one there (“Tool manager …”).
va.schrittweite.tooltip: How far the spiral advances along the bar per revolution – at most the cutter diameter. Empty: the grey suggestion, ae of the application from the tool table.
va.aufmass_schlichten.tooltip: This much stays all round after finishing – 0 finishes the part.
va.schlichten.schon: The job already has “{name}” – double-click it to change it.
va.rund: {art}: “All-round roughing” calculates as with an end mill of the same diameter – the part stays safe. Between the turns of the spiral, ridges up to {rille} mm above the allowance remain; less feed per revolution makes them flatter.
va.lage.nicht_radial: {werkzeug} does not sit radially on {aufnahme} – the path needs it radial from {richtung} towards the axis. Give {werkzeug} a holder that stands radially in the tool manager, such as “VDI30 driven radial”.
va.lage.nicht_radial_gerade: {werkzeug} does not sit radially on {aufnahme} – the path needs it radial from {richtung} towards the axis. {aufnahme} itself stands radially: give {werkzeug} a straight holder in the tool manager.
va.lage.kein_platz: “{maschine}” has no station for {werkzeug} – “Check on machine” skips it.
va.lage.nicht_bestueckt: {werkzeug} is in no station of “{maschine}” – load it under “Tool loading” in “Edit machine”. Otherwise the program calls it by its number, and “Check on machine” says what sits there.
va.rund.ohne_rillen: {art}: “All-round roughing” calculates as with an end mill of the same diameter – the part stays safe; at this feed per revolution no ridges remain.
va.uebernehmen.tooltip: Changes the operation: cutter, application and the values below – one undo step. A tool controller that no operation uses afterwards is removed.
va.aendern.text: You are changing an existing machining: the cutter, the application and the values below apply after “Apply”. Speed and feed belong to the application in the tool manager – change and save them there, then “Apply”.
va.aendern.werkzeug_fehlt: The cutter of this machining (“{controller}”) is not on offer here – it is missing from the tool manager or has no cutting data there for this material. “Apply” uses the selected one.
va.aendern.zurueck: “Back” leads to bar, centre and rotary axis as they are in the job.
va.aendern.rohteil_fest: Bar and position can no longer be changed here: the job no longer looks as the wizard created it (stock or part changed by hand).
va.aendern.anderes_teil: While changing, the part stays “{teil}” – for another part create a new job: click its end face, then “4-axis machining”.
vs.name: All-round finishing {werkzeug}
vs.eigenschaft.schrittweite: Stepover: feed per revolution of the spiral, along the bar – at most the cutter diameter.
vs.eigenschaft.aufmass: Allowance: this much stays all round after finishing (0: finished).
vs.eigenschaft.kammhoehe: Height of the ridge left between two turns of the spiral, on a face square to the cutter (calculated).
vs.eigenschaft.umdrehungen: Number of turns of the spiral (calculated).
vs.eigenschaft.vorstufen: How often finishing first passes where roughing left more than the radius of its cutter – each pass at most that deep (calculated).
vs.fehler.form: The add-on does not know the shape of this tool (thread mill, drill …) – choose a ball, torus or flat end mill for finishing.
vs.fehler.ohne_schruppen: The job has no “All-round roughing” – without it, finishing would take the whole bar in one pass.
rw.werkzeug_radial: “{operation}”: the path is calculated for a tool pointing radially at the axis from {richtung} – but {werkzeug} on {aufnahme} sits differently. Run like this, it does not fit the part: give {werkzeug} a holder in the tool manager that stands radially (such as “VDI30 driven radial”), or use a station pointing from {richtung}.
rw.werkzeug_radial_gerade: “{operation}”: the path is calculated for a tool pointing radially at the axis from {richtung} – but {werkzeug} on {aufnahme} sits differently. Run like this, it does not fit the part: {aufnahme} itself stands radially – give {werkzeug} a straight holder in the tool manager.
dialog.verfahrweg.lage_nur_von: At the “from” limit it is {von}; “to” has no limit.
dialog.verfahrweg.lage_nur_bis: At the “to” limit it is {bis}; “from” has no limit.
dialog.grenze.tooltip: How far the axis may move – the limit on the assembly joint. Empty: no limit.
dialog.verfahrweg.null: Counted as on the joint: the position of the slide, not the tool tip.
dialog.schwenkbereich.null: Counted as on the joint, in degrees; does not apply while “endless” is ticked.
dialog.verfahrweg.lage: {achse} is now at {stellung}; {aufnahme} is {abstand} away from the workpiece mount (along {achse}).
dialog.verfahrweg.lage_grenzen: At the limits it is {von} and {bis}.
dialog.verfahrweg.spitze: Where the tip gets to with a tool is shown by “Check on machine”.
